Links: [{"title":"Korea Pro - South Korea news and analysis on politics, business and culture","url":"https://koreapro.org/"},{"title":"Korean Peninsula Update, October 7, 2026","url":"https://www.aei.org/commentary/korean-peninsula-update-october-7-2026/"},{"title":"Today's Major News (October 6, 2026)","url":"https://news.sbs.co.kr/english/article.do?news_id=N1008784768"},{"title":"South Korea: Latest News and Updates","url":"https://www.scmp.com/topics/south-korea"},{"title":"South Korea","url":"https://www.aljazeera.com/where/south-korea/"},{"title":"South Korea: News & Insights - Nikkei Asia","url":"https://asia.nikkei.com/location/east-asia/south-korea"},{"title":"2026 in South Korean television","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_in_South_Korean_television"},{"title":"Armed Forces Day (South Korea)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_Day_(South_Korea)"},{"title":"Veterans Day (South Korea)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veterans_Day_(South_Korea)"}]

Here's what the search turned up for South Korea in October 2026. The most recent dated items are from around October 13–17, 2026.

**Politics and government**
- South Korea's Cabinet vetting crises expose decades of presidential resets, a feature by Joon Ha Park dated October 14, looks at how past presidents responded to nomination disputes, up to the latest reshuffle.
- The National Assembly's parliamentary audit begins today for a run of about a month. (SBS, October 6)

**Security and North Korea**
- A landmine explosion injured three South Korean soldiers in the Korean Demilitarized Zone, and S Korea demands apology over DMZ blasts as N Korea denies planting mines.
- Seoul's response has been measured. Unification Minister Chung Dong-young said on October 2 that Seoul must not show hostility toward Pyongyang, while conservative opposition is pressing for military countermeasures.
- North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles towards the sea, and South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said one of the missiles flew more than 900km.
- North Korea says it tested a new torpedo with AI tech (SCMP, October 17).
- South Korea's NIS reported that North Korea recently transferred ballistic missiles to Russia for the first time in approximately one year.

**Diplomacy**
- South Korea to recall Ukraine envoy in diplomatic row over POWs (Al Jazeera, October 8).
- South Korea pledges legal action over alleged fuel exports to Russia, according to the same Al Jazeera listing.

**Economy and markets**
- South Korea bets on Egypt as export hub despite rising financial risks.
- South Korea's stock rout raises doubts over durability of chip windfall, with a five-day KOSPI sell-off reported on October 14.
- The won faces pressure as foreign bond buying loses momentum, and the WGBI entry is set to end in November.

**Society, crime, and other news**
- In response to recent consecutive hacking incidents in the financial sector, Prime Minister Han Sung-sook has ordered a complete overhaul of security systems.
- The Justice Ministry has apologised after the Incheon suspect met his probation officer hours before the shopping centre rampage. The stabbing on October 13 injured eight people.
- South Korea signals military exemption cuts for athletes after Asian Games (October 7).
- Space: Nuri, South Korea's space launch vehicle set for its fifth flight carrying 15 satellites, was moved to the launch pad ahead of its scheduled launch in early October.

Some sources in these results have inconsistent dates, and the search did not confirm final outcomes for several stories, such as the Nuri launch result and the DMZ investigation. If you want, I can run a narrower search on any one of these topics.

Web search results for query: "한국 주요 뉴스 2026년 10월"

Links: [{"title":"2026년 10월 1일 뉴스 - 이투데이","url":"https://www.etoday.co.kr/sitemap/?year=2026&month=10"},{"title":"2026 South Korean by-elections","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_South_Korean_by-elections"},{"title":"BIG KINDS 뉴스빅데이터 분석서비스","url":"https://www.bigkinds.or.kr/"},{"title":"이번 주, 무엇이 남았나 ｜ 2026년 10월 12일~18일 < 기획·특집 < 기사본문 - 데일리25","url":"https://www.daily25news.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=7943"},{"title":"[한국뉴스 TV] 26년 10월 15일 (목) 오늘의 주요뉴스 < 오늘의 주요뉴스 < 한국뉴스TV < 기사본문 - 한국뉴스","url":"https://www.24news.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=310787"},{"title":"[한국뉴스 TV] 26년 10월 16일 (금) 오늘의 주요뉴스 < 오늘의 주요뉴스 < 한국뉴스TV < 기사본문 - 한국뉴스","url":"https://www.24news.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=310873"},{"title":"brunch.co.kr","url":"https://brunch.co.kr/@35e8cb4b4cac47c/1445"},{"title":"오늘의뉴스 7JRuWn2K","url":"https://www.teamblind.com/kr/post/오늘의뉴스-7JRuWn2K"},{"title":"오늘의뉴스 NaXc0o1L","url":"https://www.teamblind.com/kr/post/오늘의뉴스-NaXc0o1L"}]

10월 중순 한국 뉴스는 **증시 급락**과 **반도체·AI 경기**가 가장 큰 흐름이었습니다. 검색된 자료는 주로 10월 12~18일과 15~16일 주간 정리이며, 일부 자료는 날짜가 명확하지 않아 제외했습니다.

**1. 증시 급락과 서킷브레이커**
- 10월 13일 코스피가 5.5% 급락해 장중 6,000선이 무너졌습니다. 이틀 뒤인 15일에는 반도체주 중심의 매도가 번지면서 시장 전체 거래를 일시 멈추는 서킷브레이커가 발동됐습니다. 13일 코스피는 5.5% 급락하며 장중 6,000선이 무너졌다. 이틀 뒤인 15일에는 반도체주를 중심으로 매도세가 확산하면서 시장 전체 거래를 일시 중단하는 서킷브레이커가 발동됐다.
- 데이터센터와 반도체 설비 투자금이 실제 수익으로 얼마나 빨리 회수될지에 대한 우려가 주가 급락의 배경으로 지목됐습니다 (대규모 데이터센터와 반도체 설비에 투입되는 자금이 실제 수익으로 얼마나 빠르게 회수될 수 있는지에 대한 우려가 커지면서).

**2. 경제 전망**
- 이형일 부총리는 반도체 호황이 내년까지 이어지며 수요가 공급을 웃돈다고 밝혔습니다 (이형일 부총리 "반도체 호황 내년까지…수요가 공급 웃돌아").
- 3대 신용평가사는 반도체·AI 호황이 한국 성장 둔화 우려를 상쇄한다고 평가했습니다 (3대 신평사 "반도체·AI 호황, 한국 성장 둔화 우려 상쇄").
- 환율도 주목받았습니다. 10월 1일 원·달러 NDF는 3.95원 올랐고 미국 30년 국채금리는 5.6%를 넘었습니다 (원·달러 NDF 3.95원 상승, 미 30년 금리 5.6% 돌파).
- 부동산 쪽에서는 비거주 1주택에 대한 세 부담 강화를 두고 거래 위축 우려가 나왔습니다 (“비거주 1주택 세 부담 강화 부적절”…전문가들 “거래 위축 우려”).

**3. 사회·안전**
- 인천의 한 복합상가에서 전자발찌를 찬 남성이 흉기를 휘둘러 여러 시민이 다쳤습니다 (인천의 한 복합상가에서는 전자발찌를 착용한 남성이 흉기를 휘둘러 여러 시민이 다쳤다.).
- 10월 2일부터 개정 형사소송법이 시행됐습니다 (개정 형소법 10월 2일 시행…전북경찰청, 수사인력 52명 보강).

**4. 정치·외교·안보**
- 6월 3일 치러진 재보궐선거는 14개 선거구의 공석을 채우는 대규모 선거였고, 그중 13석은 더불어민주당 소속 의원이 물러난 자리였습니다 (The by-elections were called due to the vacancies of 14 constituencies in the National Assembly, making the by-elections the most large-scale ones since democratisation). 이 자료는 영문 위키백과라 10월 뉴스는 아닙니다.
- 중동 전쟁을 둘러싼 한국의 군사적 역할이 다시 논쟁이 됐습니다 (국제사회에서는 중동 전쟁을 둘러싼 한국의 군사적 역할이 다시 논쟁의 대상이 됐다.).
- 북한과 중국 사이의 경제 교류도 구체화됐습니다. 압록강에서는 사람과 물자가 이동할 수 있는 통로가 실제로 열렸습니다 (사람과 물자가 이동할 수 있는 통로가 실제로 열린 것이다.).
- 국정감사가 진행 중이며, 재외동포청 이전 문제를 두고 지역 정치권의 입장이 엇갈리고 있습니다 (재외동포청 이전 논란, 국회의원 9명 / 군수·구청장 / 지역 정치인들의 입장 주목).

**5. 스포츠·행사**
- 전국체전에서 역도 손현호 선수가 또 3관왕에 오르며 한국신기록을 세웠습니다 ([전국체전] 역도, 손현호 또 3관왕 ‘번쩍’…한국신기록도).
- KIA 타이거즈는 준플레이오프 1차전에서 승리했습니다 (KIA 네일·김도영, ‘믿음’으로 준PO 1차전 승리 합작).

**참고:** 이 결과는 뉴스 요약 사이트와 집계 페이지 위주라 원문 기사에서 세부 수치를 한 번 더 확인하는 것이 좋습니다. 특정 분야(증시, 정치, 스포츠 등)를 더 깊이 알고 싶으면 말씀해 주세요.

Yes, the KOSPI hit a circuit breaker on October 15, 2026, though the sources disagree on some details.

- **The trigger:** Digital Times reported that the market fell on concerns about AI investment profitability and credit risk. Circuit breakers were triggered for 20 minutes each on the KOSDAQ (12:23) and the KOSPI market (12:38) on the 15th, halting trading.
- **Derivatives:** Trading in derivatives based on both market indices, including KOSPI 200 and KOSDAQ 150 futures and options, was also completely suspended.
- **Closing levels:** Etoday reported that the KOSPI plunged 8.06% to close at 5,524.53 and the KOSDAQ fell 8.01% to close at 757.92.

- **Resumption:** When trading resumes, price limits will be expanded in the downward direction for futures and for options (calls down, puts up), and continuous trading will normalize following a 10-minute order collection and single-price auction.

The sources conflict on several points. Digital Times gives the KOSPI halt at 12:38 p.m., while Etoday's timing is not in the excerpt I retrieved. The 5,524.53 close from Etoday also sits well below the 6,869.83 close reported for August 18, so that figure would need confirming against an official Korea Exchange source. I'd recommend checking the Korea Exchange or Yonhap for the authoritative timeline and closing figures.

The blast happened on September 21, 2026, and Seoul has since attributed it to North Korean mines and demanded an apology. Pyongyang denies responsibility.

**The incident:** Three South Korean troops were hurt in the blast, which occurred inside the DMZ. Three South Korean officers were severely injured in the September 21 explosion inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ), the heavily mined buffer dividing the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice. One lost his foot. Casualty details vary between reports. A later Korea Times account says two of the victims remain hospitalized with serious injuries, while a third is receiving treatment for less significant wounds.

**Seoul's demand:** The Joint Chiefs of Staff said "This is a clear violation of the Armistice Agreement and undermines the spirit of existing inter-Korean agreements; it must be stopped immediately," he said, adding "we strongly urge an apology and responsible measures."

**North Korea's response:** Hours earlier, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un had denied North Korea was behind the landmine blasts. South Korea's assertion is "too low and dirty as befitting the tribes of the ROK," Kim Yo Jong, said in a statement carried by state news agency KCNA.

**The investigation:** A joint South Korea–UN Command investigation reached its conclusion in early October. The conclusion came after a joint on-site investigation with the United Nations Command and forensic analysis by the National Forensic Service. The National Forensic Service said fragments from the injured soldiers matched North Korean plastic anti-personnel mines collected from the Imjin River. Seoul's military said the mines were planted south of the MDL under the pretext of so-called 'border fortification' work by North Korea.

**Next steps:** South Korea is weighing measures to force an apology from North Korea over a recent landmine blast that wounded three soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) between the two countries, a Defence Ministry spokesperson has said. The military has also said it would keep clearing mines on its side. Seoul would continue removing North Korean mines south of the MDL unless the North did so voluntarily.

**Context:** Landmine incidents have happened before. In 2015, two South Korean soldiers were seriously wounded in a landmine blast on the southern side of the DMZ, with one losing both legs. Seoul concluded at the time that North Korean troops had crossed the MDL to plant the mines, an accusation Pyongyang denied.

The Justice Ministry apologised after a knife attack at a shopping complex in Incheon on Tuesday, 13 October 2026, by a man who was wearing an electronic ankle monitor.

**The attack:** The man is 59, according to AP reporting. A 59-year-old man stabbed at least eight people Tuesday at a shopping mall in the South Korean city of Incheon. The suspect moved between floors on an escalator before shoppers threw chairs at him and subdued him. A woman in her 20s suffered cardiac arrest and underwent emergency surgery but had not regained consciousness.

**The apology:** The ministry said in a statement that it "We deeply apologise for causing great concern to the public over today's knife attack in Incheon involving an individual subject to electronic monitoring". It also said it was conducting a "thorough investigation into the circumstances of the incident and the entire electronic monitoring and supervision process". Another report says the ministry acknowledged the monitoring system failed to prevent the attack and promised a review of its supervision, treatment and risk assessment, along with a broader review of electronic monitoring and parole management (The Justice Ministry apologised publicly, acknowledging the monitoring system failed to prevent the attack).

**Background on the suspect:** He served a sentence for attempted murder over a 2015 attack on his ex-wife. He was then ordered to wear an electronic ankle monitor for 10 years after serving his sentence and was barred from leaving his home between midnight and 6:00am. Police also investigated him last month for allegedly puncturing a protest sign outside a hospital with a kitchen knife (he was also investigated last month on suspicion of carrying a weapon after allegedly using a kitchen knife to puncture a protest sign outside a hospital in Incheon).

**Conflicting accounts:** The ministry said the device was not tampered with. The ministry said there had been no attempt to damage the monitoring device and no breach of its conditions connected with the attack. However, one report says he had previously been punished for breaching restrictions on leaving his home while wearing the device. The sources do not reconcile this, so treat it as unresolved.

**Government response:** President Lee Jae-myung, visiting an Incheon police agency, demanded a swift and thorough investigation and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

South Korea's government responded to a string of bank data breaches in early October 2026, and the Prime Minister and President both issued orders.

**The breaches:** Prime Minister Han Sung-sook addressed the issue on October 6. Shinhan Bank disclosed a personal information leak affecting approximately 25,000 people on October 1, and KB Kookmin Bank and Hana Bank were subsequently found to have experienced data breaches. Second-tier institutions such as Yegaram Savings Bank were also hit.

**Prime Minister's response:** Han urged police to act quickly. Her remarks came alongside a call for a complete overhaul of the certification system. She said the attacks are presumed to have used artificial intelligence, and AI-enabled phishing could cause secondary damage. She also warned that similar methods could spread into the industrial sector and government or public areas.

**Presidential directives:** At a Cabinet meeting on October 6, President Lee Jae Myung ordered the government to dedicate personnel and resources to minimizing damage from the attacks at financial firms. The breaches exposed customer information at seven companies, including Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank. Police launched an investigation with a 28-member team, and Lee called for stronger preventive cybersecurity and faster development of AI security tools. According to one report, he also ordered an inspection of security systems across national core infrastructure and the private sector.

**Regulatory action:** One report says the Financial Services Commission held an emergency meeting with banks, credit companies, and financial regulators to order an inspection of defense systems against unauthorized access. The Financial Supervisory Service has since launched on-site inspections of Shinhan Bank and KB Kookmin Bank.

**Context:** One report places these incidents within a larger run of cyber incidents, noting that a former employee forged internal authentication keys and accessed the personal information of approximately 37.5 million people at Coupang between April and November 2025.

**Caveats:** The sources I found mostly cover the October 6 announcements. I did not find reporting on a formal, detailed security overhaul plan or its timeline, so the "overhaul" language may refer mainly to the certification system and inspections. The Coupang figures and the inspection details come from a single less-established site, so treat them with some caution. For ongoing developments, check Yonhap, Korea Times, or the Financial Services Commission directly.
